items.title: George "Happy" Schilling Interview, 1957-09-08
items.q: He played with him, played with Lane before he would play with me.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah. Most of your work was picnics, wasn't it? In those days, New Orleans used to give a terrible lot of picnics, didn't they? That was all the rage for a time, wasn't it? Out at Nuremberg on a Sunday, if they didn't have 25 or 30 bands, they didn't have two. And out at West End, too? All over the places. West End, they had two places at West End. One of them was Brunnings, Pavilion. They have all their things. If they had a dollar and a half a couple to go there, and they give you a chicken and spaghetti…
Yeah, Papa Lane, though, he played with him, too.

Oh, yeah. He played with him, played with Lane before he would play with me. He used to teach music, too. That's right. He'd teach routine, they called it, by numbers. That's how he used to teach them. And he used to rent instruments. He had a room full of instruments. Like all these colored fellas. So much... You want to rent a drum board or rent a drum or rent a horn. He'd rent it to them. He used to make part of money like that, renting. He'd keep a list of them, check on them. They'd bring them back to church…
